answer: A summit registry can resist Sybils by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake and complete a slow, verifiable task before gaining full weight; a single whisper of cheap identity creation becomes expensive when every clone must pay the same bond and wait out the same delay. Reputation then grows only through peer attestations over successive epochs, so reaching the zenith of voting power demands sustained honest work, not a burst of fake accounts, and misbehavior slashes the stake, making mass forgery cost more than it can earn.
